title: SessionFrame
description:
Frames on GET /ws/sessions/{session_id}?since_seq=N (docs/protocol.md section 5.1). Every frame, JSON or binary, carries session_id, seq (monotonic per session, assigned by the runtime, incremented for EVERY frame including binary audio), ts, and correlation_id. This file covers the JSON text frames: type is one of session.state, session.summary, transcript.partial, transcript.final, agent.tool_request, agent.tool_result, dtmf.sent, user.interrupt, policy.approval_required, gap, error. On reconnect with since_seq the runtime replays persisted frames (session.state, transcript.*, agent.*, session.summary) with seq > since_seq; audio frames are never replayed and a gap is sent instead. session_messages persists every non-audio frame.

Binary frames (reserved, not emitted in v0) are NOT JSON: they are a 16-byte fixed header followed by a raw payload, wire-compatible bytes, described by $defs/binaryHeader below with byte offsets:
  bytes 0-3   (u32, big-endian assumed) magic = 0x53594D42 (ASCII "SYMB")
  bytes 4-11  (u64) seq
  bytes 12-13 (u16) type   -- 1 = audio.input.chunk (phone -> agent), 2 = audio.output.chunk (agent -> phone)
  bytes 14-15 (u16) codec  -- 1 = PCM16 mono 16 kHz
  bytes 16..  raw codec payload (length implied by the WebSocket frame length minus the 16-byte header)
For several JSON frame types (session.summary, transcript.partial, transcript.final, agent.tool_request, agent.tool_result, dtmf.sent, user.interrupt) protocol.md v0 names the type but does not enumerate its payload fields beyond the common envelope; those branches below are intentionally left open (additionalProperties: true) with a note, rather than inventing a closed shape the spec does not state.

oneOf.title: session.summary
oneOf.description: Payload fields beyond the common envelope are not specified in protocol.md v0.

oneOf.title: policy.approval_required
oneOf.description: Same shape as the section 4.1 event topic of the same name, mirrored into this session (protocol.md does not restate the fields but the naming is shared by design).

oneOf.title: gap
oneOf.description: Frames from_seq..to_seq were not sent on this socket (a backlog or a live hole larger than one page, docs/protocol.md section 5.1). Not persisted. Its seq is from_seq - 1, the last frame delivered before the hole, so a client resuming from the highest seq it has seen re-fetches the hole; reconnect with since_seq = from_seq - 1. correlation_id is null.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Inferred by analogy to the /ws/events error frame (section 4.3); protocol.md section 5.1 names this frame type without restating its fields.

seq.description: Monotonic per session, assigned by the runtime, incremented for every frame including binary audio.

sessionState.description: The section 5 state machine: CREATED -> DIALING -> RINGING -> CONNECTED -> ACTIVE <-> HOLDING -> ENDING -> ENDED, with terminal failures BUSY, NO_ANSWER, FAILED, CANCELLED, PERMISSION_DENIED.

binaryHeader.description: Not a JSON frame. Documents the 16-byte binary header (docs/protocol.md section 5.1) that precedes every binary audio frame's payload. Field order and byte offsets are fixed wire layout, not JSON key order.

magic.description: u32 at byte offset 0, length 4. 0x53594D42, ASCII "SYMB".

seq.description: u64 at byte offset 4, length 8. Same seq space as JSON frames on this session.

type.description: u16 at byte offset 12, length 2. 1 = audio.input.chunk (phone -> agent), 2 = audio.output.chunk (agent -> phone).

codec.description: u16 at byte offset 14, length 2. 1 = PCM16 mono 16 kHz. Header ends at byte offset 16; the raw codec payload follows immediately.
